new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Protection of the environment, forests and wildlife appears both as a Directive Principle and as a Fundamental Duty.
2. Free legal aid is a Fundamental Duty of every citizen under Article 51A.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Environment is in DPSP Article 48A (duty of the State) and FD Article 51A(g) (duty of citizens). Free legal aid is DPSP Article 39A, not a Fundamental Duty.
new.angle: U0289 #14 DPSP vs FD vs both

new.s: Which of the following is found in the Directive Principles but has no matching Fundamental Duty in Article 51A?
o: Preserving the heritage of composite culture
Equal justice and free legal aid
new.x: Free legal aid is only a Directive Principle (Article 39A). Environment (51A(g)), heritage (51A(f)) and education (51A(k)) also appear as Fundamental Duties.
new.angle: U0289 #14 DPSP vs FD vs both

new.s: Which of the following is a Directive Principle and NOT a Fundamental Right under the Constitution?
o: Right to education for children aged 6-14
new.x: The right to work is a Directive Principle under Article 41, not a Fundamental Right. Education for 6-14 (Art. 21A), forced labour ban (Art. 23) and equality (Art. 14) are Fundamental Rights.

new.s: 9 November, the day the Legal Services Authorities Act came into force in 1995, is observed as:
new.x: The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 came into force on 9 November 1995, so 9 November is National Legal Services Day.

new.s: The National Legal Services Authority (NALSA), which organises Lok Adalats, gives effect to which Directive Principle?
new.x: NALSA was formed under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, which implements Article 39A on equal justice and free legal aid.
new.angle: U0289 PYQ yf9867a003dd NALSA / legal aid

new.s: Which part of the Constitution may be used to decide the scope of both the Fundamental Rights and the Directive Principles?
new.x: The Preamble states the aims of the Constitution, so it may be used to decide the ambit of both Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.
new.angle: U0290 PYQ y5bfb8896ac3 Preamble and FR/DPSP scope

new.s: Which of the following cases concerned personal liberty under Article 21 rather than property rights or the amending power?
new.x: Maneka Gandhi widened Article 21 by requiring a fair, just and reasonable procedure. Golaknath and Kesavananda dealt with property and amending power; Sanjeev Coke with Article 39(b).

new.s:
Arrange the following cases in chronological order:
A. Minerva Mills
B. In re Kerala Education Bill
C. Sanjeev Coke
D. Golaknath
new.x: Kerala Education Bill (1958), Golaknath (1967), Minerva Mills (1980), Sanjeev Coke (1983).

new.s: The idea of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Constitution of:
new.x: Fundamental Duties were taken from the Constitution of the former Soviet Union (USSR). Japan only has a comparable list; Ireland is the source of DPSPs.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of constitutional feature and source country is correctly matched?
new.x: Fundamental Duties come from the former USSR, Directive Principles from Ireland and Fundamental Rights from the USA.

new.s: In which year was the eleventh Fundamental Duty, Article 51A(k), added to the Constitution?
new.x: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 added Article 51A(k), raising the number of duties from 10 to 11.
new.angle: U0291 #12 Eleventh duty -> amendment and year

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Article 51A(k):
1. It was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
2. It is addressed to parents or guardians of children aged 6 to 14 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: the 86th Amendment (2002) added 51A(k), the only duty addressed to parents or guardians, to give education to children aged 6-14.
new.angle: U0291 #12 Eleventh duty -> amendment and year

new.s: The Swaran Singh Committee of 1976, which recommended Fundamental Duties, was set up by:
new.x: The Congress party set up the Swaran Singh Committee in 1976, during the Internal Emergency of 1975-77.
new.angle: U0291 #2 Swaran Singh Committee - set up by

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the 106th Amendment (women's reservation):
1. The reservation starts only after delimitation based on the first Census taken after its commencement.
2. The reservation lasts 15 years and cannot be extended by Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The quota begins only after delimitation on the first Census after commencement. It lasts 15 years but Parliament can extend it by law, so statement 2 is wrong.

new.s:
Match the amendments with their changes:
A. 12th Amendment
B. 15th Amendment
C. 58th Amendment
D. 96th Amendment
1. Authoritative Hindi text of the Constitution
2. 'Oriya' changed to 'Odia'
3. Goa, Daman and Diu made a Union Territory
4. Retirement age of High Court judges raised from 60 to 62
new.x: 12th (1962) made Goa, Daman and Diu a UT; 15th (1963) raised HC judges' retirement age to 62; 58th (1987) gave the Hindi text; 96th (2011) changed Oriya to Odia.

new.s: The 97th Amendment made the right to form co-operative societies a Fundamental Right by amending Article:
new.x: The 97th Amendment (2011) added co-operative societies to Article 19(1)(c); Article 43B is the Directive Principle it added.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Part IXB (co-operative societies):
1. A co-operative board can have a maximum of 21 directors.
2. The accounts must be audited within six months of the close of the financial year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: Article 243ZJ caps the board at 21 directors, and audit must be done within six months of the end of the financial year.
